items.title: Bind Epic G consumers to current E/F approvals and catalog roles
items.impact: Prevents false fit and competing catalog authority
items.deps: Current E classifications/identities, exact owner release and F binding; no formal F closure.
items.problem: Historical E/F registers preserve candidate or superseded states. G needs current class, relationship, publication and freshness checks before extending customer surfaces.
items.outcome: One additive G eligibility/readiness contract consuming E approval and F reconciliation, with automated current-state evidence. Document continued default-template use and proposed route ownership.
scope: Reuse rhino.product_class, compatible_machines, E exact identities, granted values and receipt lifecycle; keep fit/included/optional/recommended meanings distinct.
Produce read-only per-class/Variant SKU, price, inventory, media, resource and attribute-readiness reports. Include all 111 G Products, including the 72 with no fit.
Compare exact full reference lists and source/target visibility, schema/type, source digest and time; reject orphan, duplicate, unknown-class, unsupported/inferred or stale edges.
Record ADR-0001's nonmachine template proposals as unnecessary for the evidenced MVP, in a bounded follow-up decision; do not require a new template or registry.
out: Creating definitions/values/Products; F signoff; approval renewal by reading; consumer feature implementation; catalog normalization.
ac: Current live read reconciles all Product/Variant GIDs and class values without title/tag/type inference; complete pagination and failures are explicit.
Every eligible fit value matches an approved current exact set; JadeMaster nine edges remain data-approved but customer-link ineligible; Saw Vice two edges absent.
Unknown/changed/expired references fail closed with a reason; missing SKU/media/resources are reported separately from fit eligibility.
Evidence validates current-source digests and read-only operation inventory; freshness cannot be extended merely by regenerating a report.
items.handoff: Extend existing scripts/lib/epic-e-readiness.js, epic-f-consumer.js and owner-release conventions only where appropriate; create G-specific adapters/assertions rather than modifying immutable F receipts. Add meaningful negative fixtures. Discovery harnesses are observational inputs, not a completed contract.
items.success: 122 Products and 125 Variants accounted for; zero unsupported eligibility grants; deterministic failure reasons.
items.risks: Treating historical candidates or public metafield existence as approval; silently renewing receipt; making optional missing data universal blockers.
items.validation: Unit checks for exact multi-machine lists, revoked/expired grants, unpublished targets, class drift and orphan handles; schema/read-only query checks; compare current Admin against approved source.
items.human: None for architecture/current read. E owner approval remains mandatory for future new values, outside this PBI.
items.automation: Read-only drift refresh, classification coverage, SKU/media gap reports, exact reference-set and no-inferred-fit assertions.
items.blockers: No blocking owner question for G1. F historical stale prose must not override the current bound release.

items.title: Keep ordinary Product detail safe and show SKU only when useful
items.area: Default Product template and native commerce
items.impact: Preserves buying and improves identity without a new template
items.deps: G-PBI-001. Price decisions in 006 are independent per Product; no SKU population prerequisite.
items.problem: The existing default template works, but empty SKU containers announce no useful identifier; missing image/description pages have little context. Cloning machine templates would add complexity.
items.outcome: One default Product experience retains native identity, price, Variant/quantity/purchase and availability; blank content collapses, real approved SKUs display and update by selection.
scope: Use templates/product.json and shared main-product with governed class conditions; no machine-page layout transplant.
Suppress the whole SKU row when native SKU is blank; show a named/copyable selectable value when an approved issued SKU exists; never display registry proposals as native values.
Preserve native current-market purchase state, errors, price, quantity and Variant URL; retain four Size options as native commerce data.

Keep existing permissible images/prose; collapse missing modules; use neutral Contact/product URL for support when facts/resources are unavailable. Target identity media alt behavior only where useful, without wholesale new content.
Address observed zero-size native lightbox controls with usable native interaction or an intentional plain-image state; preserve machine gallery containment.
out: New class templates, SKU assignment/allocation, pricing changes, marketing rewrite, stock policy, parsed dimensions, new images or unapproved instructions.
ac: Available item remains orderable through existing controls; sold-out item stays disabled; do not override native state with Admin aggregate quantities.
Blank SKU produces no empty visible/accessibility announcement; populated approved fixture updates exact SKU with selected Variant.
Saw Blade 6/8/14/18 selections retain exact Variant IDs and $15/$25/$75/$125 baseline prices unless current Admin changes legitimately.
No-media/no-description/no-fit pages have no empty headings or broken controls; approved native media remains available.
Machine template behavior, existing F fact/media containment and native Related products semantics remain intact.
Configured image interaction is usable by keyboard/pointer, or inaccessible empty controls are omitted for a plain-image presentation; no new gallery architecture.
items.handoff: Reuse main-product block implementation and native product-info update lifecycle; guard classes with the current role contract. Preserve original SKU issuer and E registry. Do not turn anonymous Shopify IDs or legacy aliases into displayed SKUs.
items.success: All three G roles pass native purchase/empty-content checks; zero empty SKU rows; no Product template assignment writes.
items.risks: A shared-section edit can regress F or Variant updates; hiding whole Product information because optional content is absent.
items.validation: Browser available/unavailable, native Variant/quantity, empty/populated SKU, missing media/description fixtures; run product-template and current F guard checks appropriate to changed shared files.
items.human: No new data decision required for blank-safe behavior. Real SKU values remain E-approved allocation work; targeted $0 decisions in 006.
items.automation: Product-role page assertions, native control regression, SKU update/blank assertions and media inventory report.
items.consumers: G-003/005/007; J checkout; L support; O future reorder.

items.title: Render approved Fits these machines on existing G Product pages
items.impact: Lets a buyer confirm an exact approved machine match
items.deps: G-PBI-001 and shared page integration with G-PBI-002; current E approval/receipt and publication.
items.problem: Ordinary Product pages do not surface their approved compatible_machines references, even when exact fit has been reconciled.
items.outcome: A small conditional forward-fit module on the default Product template links only current eligible exact machines.
scope: Consume approved full Product-reference lists directly, with E/F eligibility, current source/target identity, class, visibility and freshness checks.
Allow one-to-many matches; preserve the clamp's two targets; distinguish unavailable targets from unknown fit internally.
Withhold unknown, removed, unapproved, unpublished or expired relationships; do not emit an empty fit heading. A neutral Contact link may provide recovery.
Label links as approved fit only; keep Related products and included/optional/recommended information semantically separate.
out: New compatibility assertions, family-derived matches, negative-fit claims, dimension matching, Saw Vice split, approval of JadeMaster publication, a general selector/filter service.
ac: All eligible current published-target edges render once in deterministic order; exact list/value comparison is enforced before any claim.
The clamp links SawMaster 18 and 24; the JadeMaster-only belt guard has no dead machine/fit link; Saw Vice has no fit claim.
Missing fit on the other 72 Products does not imply incompatible or hide purchase controls.
Expired/revoked/source-drifted approval suppresses output; source removal is reflected without stale static links.
Native link names, headings and focus order work on mobile/desktop; structured data/metadata do not introduce unsupported fit claims.
items.handoff: Use native product.metafields.rhino.compatible_machines.value plus an E/F approval-bound G consumer. A public reference is data access, not approval. Add a conditional shared snippet rather than another Product section/controller.
items.success: Zero false/dead fit links; all 31 currently eligible edges representable; no false claim for nine unpublished-target edges or two blocked Saw Vice edges.
items.risks: Highest risk: false technical compatibility from stale grants, partial-list matching or unapproved catalog observations.
items.validation: Positive single/two-machine, missing, unpublished, orphan, class mismatch, changed full set, expiry/revocation, Saw Vice suppression and keyboard/axe tests.
items.human: None for the current 40 approved edges; no extra owner worksheet. Any newly proposed relationship remains E-owned.
items.automation: Exact-edge renderer assertions and no-inferred-compatibility checks across DOM, metadata and generated projection.
items.consumers: G-004/007; O future ownership; H exact fit later.
blockers: Immediate private revocation/absolute expiry remains PARTIAL; production operating policy is not approved.

items.outcome: A narrow machine-context entry routes buyers to the existing published machine Product and its exact compatible-items section.
scope: Reuse F dependent→machine reverse output; add only necessary anchors/entry semantics and approved exact machine navigation.
Offer published machines with results; for no-known-match machines use a clear neutral state/contact and do not imply no parts exist.
Preserve current source/target grants and F lookup budget; make G indexes projection consumers, not additional relationship authorities.
Record any native named collection as general browse only unless each shown fit claim is independently edge-approved.
out: Standalone parts landing Page creation, new relationship metaobjects, collection membership rewrite, unpublished machine exposure, broad filters or comparison.
ac: Machine entry reaches an actual existing machine route/section with exactly the approved products for that machine.
Existing five reverse outputs remain complete and deduplicated; no second source of fit data is created.
JadeMaster and no-edge targets produce no dead/false fit destination; absent edges never mean no replacement exists.
EM-1 included catalog references plus reverse cards stay within the shared all_products unique-handle budget; membership expansion is bounded/tested.
Saw Vice is omitted and missing images do not prevent approved text links; ordinary Product destination remains the purchase route.
items.handoff: Reuse scripts/lib/epic-f-customer-release.js and rhino-owner-approved-context shards. Preserve immutable receipts/bindings; any source extension must use established bounded successor evidence. Prefer existing sections/anchors and the current navigation registers.
items.success: Five currently usable machine journeys; 31 reverse entries to 30 distinct Products; zero new collections/metaobjects/Pages required.
items.risks: Duplicating existing F behavior; interpreting EM-1 collection's 49 members as fit; unbounded all_products calls.
items.validation: Exact reverse-forward parity from one source; existing machine card membership regression; empty/unpublished/deleted target tests; anchor/focus and lookup-budget checks.
items.human: None for existing exact machine routes. Additional machine publication or fit approvals are separate optional dependencies.
items.automation: Reverse projection parity, target visibility/drift, link/anchor and lookup budget assertions.
items.blockers: No Saw Vice split, variable-speed LapMaster, 40-gallon TumbleMaster, F-015B or F-018B dependency.

items.title: Provide a small role index and anonymous consumable reorder entry
items.impact: Makes existing sellable Products reachable without catalog jargon
items.deps: G-PBI-001/004; G-PBI-002 native Product path; existing C/D route/navigation contracts. 006 controls affected-item commercial readiness.
items.problem: No aggregate G destination exists; the MAIN homepage/menu offers generic Catalog/Contact. Consumables beyond narrow collections are hard to reach without internal names.
items.evidence: Parts/accessories/consumables candidate collections and parts-for-my-machine Page return 404. /collections/all is live; 39 governed consumables include 42 Variants. MAIN homepage differs from local D fallback state.
items.outcome: A compact class-grouped existing-Product link index hosted on verified /collections/all, plus bounded named entry links and existing machine-context paths.
scope: Use existing /collections/all as the preferred host; three simple Product-role groups, current exact identity/class guards and native Product URLs. No invented collection/Page handles.

Integrate a single bounded collection traversal/pagination strategy; cover all current eligible items beyond the normal 50-item iteration limit; avoid 111 all_products lookups or duplicate image grids.
Connect the index and machine-context links to C/D route records, menu/theme surfaces only as needed; refresh MAIN/preview parity before a later deployment.
Keep anonymous reorder at Product/Variant/quantity level. Preserve legitimate native option selection and optional Variant URLs; maintain safe empty/changed/unpublished states.
out: Search & Discovery changes, predictive search, faceted search, full collection taxonomy, global sorting/merchandising, account history, new Page/collection creation, unrelated D homepage rollout.
ac: Each G role has a named working existing-route entry; links reach existing eligible Products without requiring SKUs, internal catalog names or account state.
Current eligible 111-Product/114-Variant inventory is fully accounted for, with any six-item commercial exclusions explicitly owner-disposed rather than silently omitted.
Role grouping uses approved class, never title/tag/type/collection inference; no group claims machine fit without a separately approved edge.
No duplicate conflicting pagers, silent truncation at 20/50, or stale links after publication/handle drift; growth beyond current count has explicit pagination behavior.
New fragments/anchors resolve before route approval; native generic catalog behavior is preserved outside the narrow surface; keyboard/mobile and no-JS link use work.
items.handoff: Read data/navigation-spec.json, global-navigation-ia.json, homepage-section-outcomes.json and D-PBI-016 record. Select bounded collection.products traversal and native pagination; verify official Liquid limits. If a new Page would become necessary, report that explicit dependency rather than creating it under this PBI. Do not claim this discovery approved new handles.
items.success: A returning buyer can reach every currently eligible consumable and select/purchase its existing Variant via an anonymous journey; no H platform introduced.
items.risks: Highest scope risk: absorbing H. Technical risks: collection pagination/20-lookup limits, duplicate grids, MAIN/local homepage drift and promoting unresolved zero prices.
items.validation: Route contract gates; complete class membership across pages; no title parsing/inferred fit; links/anchors/mobile/keyboard; native catalog behavior and source parity checks.
items.human: No business decision required to use the observed route. Six-item prices/holds in 006 affect those items, not host architecture. New Admin destination would require explicit later scope if proven necessary.
items.automation: Route/role coverage, pagination boundary, current identity/publication, anonymous reorder and homepage entry assertions.
items.consumers: C/D; G-007; O later; H later receives bounded route/role contract.
items.blockers: No approved consumables collection; addressed by an existing-route theme surface, not assumed new collection creation.
items.preservationBlocker: Two historical G3A QA PNGs overwritten by async screenshot writes; original hashes retained, external exact backup unavailable.

items.title: Resolve commercial readiness of the six published zero-price G Products
items.impact: Prevents silently treating unresolved $0 items as commercially ready
items.milestone: G1 parallel decision; G4 affected-item closure
items.deps: G-PBI-001 exact inventory; Product Owner response in the small decision packet. Later Admin writes require separately bounded authorization.
items.problem: Six active published G Products have $0 Variants, and sampled native pages allow Add to cart. Discovery cannot decide whether these are intentional free items or missing prices.
items.evidence: 6 in Trim Saw, Arbor Wrench, Automatic Feed Clamp, LapMaster Lap Bolt, MR16 LED Bulb and Saw Vice Plate Set; exact Product/Variant GIDs and current prices in docs/project/epic-g-required-decisions.md. No free-sale authority was found.
items.outcome: An explicit per-Product or whole-group disposition: intentional free sale with evidence, approved price, or scoped defer/hold. Other G work proceeds.
scope: Obtain only the six-item decision; permit explicit defer. Prefill all identities/prices; do not add catalog normalization, SKU, grit or split questions.
Bind any approved price/status/promotion disposition to exact Product and Variant IDs; keep Saw Vice price separate from compatibility split.
Prepare a bounded implementation/read-before/after validation handoff for any later required commerce or routing change; do not infer an automatic theme-wide zero-price rule.
Record affected-item readiness honestly; if owner defers an item, specify the launch boundary that implements that exclusion and verify it later.
out: Automatic repricing, blanket disabling of all $0 Products, assumed holds, inferred free gifts, creating Products or Variants, fixing unrelated prices/inventory.
ac: Every one of six current rows has an explicit owner disposition or remains visibly blocked; no unanswered row is treated as approved.
Intentional-free decisions record evidence; approved-price decisions specify exact Variant and value/currency; defers specify actual affected-item publication/purchase/promotion boundary.
A mere omission from new G navigation is not represented as disabling an already live Product purchase path.
Any subsequent authorized mutation has immediate exact before-read and after evidence; planning alone is not readiness closure.
All unrelated G PBIs can progress independently; Saw Vice split and two fit edges stay deferred.
items.handoff: Use the decision packet, native price/publication authority and J commercial handoff. Keep any execution separate from discovery. If no response, retain Product-scoped blocker and do not invent an action or certify all items ready.
items.success: Six of six rows explicitly resolved or explicitly deferred with a concrete launch boundary; no accidental free-sale readiness claim.
items.risks: Blocking all G for six rows; assuming default answer/elapsed time is approval; falsely equating promotion suppression with a real purchase hold.
items.validation: Exact price/status/publication drift checks; later authorized change reconciliation and native page state. No checkout transaction required in discovery; J owns checkout.
items.human: Required: Product Owner commercial disposition for these six only. Question already raised during discovery; unanswered means unresolved.
items.automation: Read-only zero-price exception audit keyed to exact Variant GIDs; owner-decision coverage and later before/after reconciliation.
items.consumers: G-005/007; J pricing/checkout; E catalog owner.
items.blockers: MR16 selling price/exact replacement specification deferred; Saw Vice model-to-Product/Variant structure/mapping unresolved. Both native zero-price purchase states remain commercial launch blockers.

items.title: Validate the integrated G journeys, accessibility and current-state drift
items.impact: Proves G customer paths without claiming deferred work complete
items.deps: G-PBI-001–006 at their explicit scope. Optional 008/009 and deferred 010 are not gates; price defers require explicit bounded disposition.
items.problem: F machine QA does not certify new ordinary-page fit, anonymous reorder, role coverage or native sold-out behavior. Automated no-overflow alone missed heavy header wrapping under text enlargement.
items.evidence: Discovery: 35 route cells/20 main axe runs plus interaction follow-up; no baseline overflow/axe defects observed; global header grows from 63 to 558px at 360px under 200% root text. Water Guard native availability differs from Admin aggregate.
items.outcome: Reproducible Product-role, fit/reverse, route/reorder, mobile/keyboard/accessibility and drift evidence, with inherited F release gates kept parked.
scope: Meaningful positive/negative tests for three G roles, zero/missing/multiple fit, unpublished target, stale grant, missing image/description/SKU, and exact inverse projection.
Real available/unavailable and native Saw Blade Variant/price/quantity state; selected approved-SKU fixture; no inferred inventory claims.
Validate 360/390/desktop, 200% text and browser zoom, heading/link names, visible focus, reflow/readability and safe empty states; coordinate the specific shared-chrome C issue.
Run current-source Admin/MAIN parity checks and bounded local/authorized preview checks; report evidence age and actual surface. Keep F performance-integrity and final signoff separate.
out: F-015B certification, F-018B final signoff, full-site WCAG certification, paid apps, performance recorder redesign, running real purchase transactions, post-O features.
ac: All implemented G acceptance paths have passing automated evidence, complete class/edge coverage, and no serious/critical storefront-owned accessibility issues.
Native availability tests use rendered state; no test treats Admin availableForSale or hidden Sold out labels as actual button state.
200% text/zoom checks assess readability, focus and header obstruction as well as horizontal overflow; shared C issue is resolved or explicitly scoped with evidence before G handoff.
Current source drift or expired fit receipt fails eligibility; ignored failures cannot be regenerated away.
H/I/M/N/O and parked F work are correctly handed off; 008/009/010 omissions do not falsely fail the defined G scope; commercial exceptions are explicit.
items.handoff: Reuse Playwright/axe and current F guards; avoid writing mirror tests for markup. Include all class inventory in static checks and representative real states in browser checks. Do not reuse discovery's partial first/second interaction attempts as passing certification.
items.success: Zero broken new routes, false fit claims or native-control regressions; complete G role/edge accounting and a bounded handoff ready for Epic J.
items.risks: Overstating a sample/axe pass; root-text header usability; relying on aggregate inventory; conflating test evidence with deployment permission or F closure.
items.validation: Run targeted unit/schema/drift/route/browser suites, shared template/native controls, keyboard/axe/reflow and protected machine regression. Deployment validation only in later authorized scope.
items.human: Only unresolved 006 dispositions or an actual discovered release-blocking defect; no broad worksheet.
items.automation: Integrated role/edge route coverage, invalid inferred-fit detection, Admin drift, native selected-Variant, accessible names/empty rows and mobile assertions.
items.consumers: Epic J onward; C accessibility; E/F current-source consumers; launch gate later.
items.blockers: No remaining bounded technical G4 acceptance blocker at recorded verification. G006 two commercial exceptions, G003 private revocation/production policy, G005 historical PNG exception, inherited C/F defects and production release gates remain open.

implementationScope: G-PBI-001 repository foundation only; all other PBIs remain proposed
